_what: The date each rail line OPENED FOR SERVICE, with the Board of Supervisors' own record of paying to build it kept alongside as corroboration.
_why: base/rail.json is today's network and carries no opening date, so the layer that
reads it drew at the present and nowhere else while the streets and the building
footprints beside it arrived by year from the record. That was the one inconsistency
in the century scrub: the city grew around a rail network that was always finished.
The gate is NOT a route's branding date. The F Market line was branded in 1995 and
Market Street has carried rail since the 1860s; gating the F's steel at 1995 would
leave Market bare for ninety years of a century that had five streetcar lines on it.
What is wanted is the date rail service began ON THAT ALIGNMENT.
Every line below carries the date it OPENED and, independently, the Board paying to
BUILD it. See _two_sources. Nothing here is recalled.
_predating: The map's first year is 1906. The cable lines and Market Street all carried rail
before it, so they need no date and are drawn from the first year the map draws --
the same convention `streets.ts` uses for a street the record is silent about.
This is stated rather than sourced: the scanned Journal of Proceedings begins in
1906, so the corpus CANNOT reach a franchise granted in 1878, and claiming a
citation for it would be false. California Street, Powell-Mason and Powell-Hyde are
19th-century cable franchises; Market Street's rail is older than the fire.

_source.publisher: Internet Archive, from the San Francisco Public Library deposit
_source.series: Journal of proceedings, Board of Supervisors, City and County of San Francisco
_source.enumerated_by: creator, never by title -- see pipeline/scripts/us_sf_city/MINUTES.md

J.name: J Church
J.opened_quote: The J Church streetcar line begins service on August 11, 1917
J.built_quote: For construction of Church street line, from Market street and Van Ness avenue to Sixteenth and Church streets, Section "A", Contract No. 23

K.name: K Ingleside
K.note: the record names the alignment, not the modern letter: the K runs the Twin Peaks Tunnel line, whose construction the Board was paying for in 1917-18.
K.opened_quote: The K Ingleside begins operation with the opening of the tunnel (Twin Peaks Tunnel, February 1918)
K.conflict: the 1918 Journal of Proceedings says service through the Twin Peaks tunnel 'was inaugurated in January'. A month earlier than the operator's date; both are recorded, neither is reconciled.
K.built_quote: Eaton & Smith, fifth payment, construction of Twin Peaks tunnel line, Municipal Railways, contract 95

L.name: L Taraval
L.note: the same volume carries a resolution headed "Operation of Taraval Cars from Ferry to the Beach".
L.opened_quote: Muni's L Taraval line opened to 33rd Avenue on April 12, 1919
L.built_quote: Eaton & Smith, 1st payment, construction of Taraval street line of Municipal Railways (claim dated Feb. 3, 1919)

M.name: M Ocean View
M.opened_quote: In 1925, the M Ocean View starts service through the Twin Peaks Tunnel
M.built_quote: Eaton & Smith, fourth payment, construction of track and paving, Ocean View line of Municipal Railways (claim dated August 13, 1925)

N.name: N Judah
N.note: the same volume pays for "construction of Duboce avenue Sunset tunnel", the bore the N runs through.
N.opened_quote: By 1928, the Sunset Tunnel is completed and the N Judah line begins to operate; the Sunset Tunnel opened October 21, 1928
N.built_quote: Eaton & Smith, second payment, construction of Sunset line of Municipal Railways (claim dated May 28, 1928)

T.name: T Third
T.note: the Board calling it NEW in April 2007 is the attestation; the January-March 2007 volume has no mention of it at all.
T.opened_quote: The T Third line starts operation in April 2007, following the completion of Phase 1 of the Third Street Light Rail Project
T.built_quote: 070445 [Status of the new T-Third Street MUNI line] Supervisor Elsbernd Hearing on the status of the new T-Third Street MUNI line and its impact on other services. 4/10/07

_two_sources: Each line carries two independent statements that agree.
OPENED: the operator's own published history (SFMTA, 'Muni History'), which is what
a date like '11 August 1917' can only come from -- the Board's Journal records Board
BUSINESS, not openings, and carries them only by accident.
BUILT: a construction payment, contract or claim quoted from the Journal of
Proceedings for that year, found independently by searching the OCR for payment
The two agree on the year for all six municipally built lines, which is the reason
to trust either. Where they differ they are BOTH recorded: the 1918 Journal says
service through the Twin Peaks tunnel 'was inaugurated in January' while the
operator dates the K Ingleside to February 1918. A month apart, and not reconciled
here, because nothing in the record settles it.

_muni_began.quote: On December 28, 1912, the San Francisco Municipal Railway (Muni) inaugurates streetcar service on the A and B lines along Geary Street between downtown and 33rd Avenue
_muni_began.note: Geary carries no rail today, so Muni's first line is not in this file at all. The map cannot show it.
